text: You must never usurp to yourself those conveniences and 'agremens' which are of common right; such as the best places, the best dishes, etc., but on the contrary, always decline them yourself, and offer them to others; who, in their turns, will offer them to you; so that, upon the whole, you will in your turn enjoy your share of the common right.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter LXXXVIII, to his son, London, November 3, Old Style 1749
